arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Nautilus contends the claim is not particular and distinct. It argues the claim is ambiguous after applying all interpretive tools.
Biosig contends the Federal Circuit correctly applied the definiteness test. It argues the claim provides reasonable notice of the invention's boundaries.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case concerns a patent for a heart-rate monitor. The core issue is the legal standard for patent claim definiteness. One side argues the claim is ambiguous because it allows two reasonable readings. The other side argues the claim is definite because a skilled artisan understands its scope.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Nautilus wants the court to reverse the lower court decision. It seeks a ruling that the patent claim is ambiguous and invalid.
Biosig wants the court to affirm the lower court decision. It seeks a ruling that the patent claim is definite and valid.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Nautilus argues the claim is ambiguous because it has two reasonable readings with different scopes.
Biosig argues the claim is definite because it gives a skilled artisan reasonable notice of the invention's boundaries.
